card.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbf{k}$ -vector space, and take $\mathscr{C}={\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\omega=V\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}-$. Then $B=\End_{\mathbf{k}}(V)^{\vee}$. Indeed, the category of finite-dimensional left $\End_{\mathbf{k}}(V)$ -modules is semisimple, with just one simple object up to isomorphism, namely  $V$.

Let $M$ be a set, let $\mathscr{C}={\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(M)$ be the category of finite-dimensional $M$ -graded $\mathbf{k}$ -vector spaces, and $\omega:\mathscr{C}\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ be the functor that forgets the $M$ -grading. Then $B=\mathbf{k}M$, the $\mathbf{k}$ -vector space with basis $M$, with the coalgebra structure given by

$\Delta(m)=m\otimes m,\quad\varepsilon(m)=1$

for all $m\in M$. For each $X\in\mathscr{C}$, the coaction of $B$ on $\omega(X)=X$ is the map

$X\to X\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B,\quad x\mapsto\sum_{m\in M}x_{m}\otimes m,$

where $x=\sum_{m\in M}x_{m}$ is the decomposition of $x$ into its homogeneous components.

Let $C$ be a coalgebra, and take $\mathscr{C}={\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{C}$, with $\omega$ the forgetful functor. Then there exists a canonical isomorphism $C\cong B$. Indeed, if $X\in{\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{C}$, there exists a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra $C^{\prime}\subset C$ such that the $C$ -comodule $X$ is actually a $C^{\prime}$ -comodule.22 2

In view of its importance, let us briefly recall the proof of this classical fact. Let $\delta:X\to X\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}C$ be the structure map of the $C$ -comodule $X$ and let $(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n})$ be a $\mathbf{k}$ -basis of $X$. Write $\delta(e_{j})=\sum_{i}e_{i}\otimes c_{i,j}$. Then $\Delta(c_{i,j})=\sum_{k}c_{i,k}\otimes c_{k,j}$ and $\varepsilon(c_{i,j})=\delta_{i,j}$ (Kronecker’s symbol), so $C^{\prime}$ can be chosen as the $\mathbf{k}$ -span in $C$ of the elements $c_{i,j}$. Then the coaction morphism $X\to X\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}C^{\prime}$ defines an algebra morphism $(C^{\prime})^{\vee}\to A_{X}$, hence a coalgebra morphism $B_{X}\to C^{\prime}$. Composing with the embedding $C^{\prime}\hookrightarrow C$ and passing to the limit we deduce a coalgebra morphism $B\to C$. In the reverse direction, if $C^{\prime}\subset C$ is a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra, then $C^{\prime}$ is an object in ${\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{C}$, hence it acquires a canonical $B$ -comodule structure, i.e. a coalgebra map $C^{\prime}\to C^{\prime}\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B$. Composing with the map induced by $\varepsilon$ we deduce a coalgebra morphism $C^{\prime}\to B$. Since $C$ is the direct limit of its finite-dimensional subcoalgebras, we deduce a coalgebra morphism $C\to B$. It is easily seen that the morphisms we constructed are inverse to each other, proving our claim.

An homomorphism of $\mathbf{k}$ -coalgebras $f:B\to C$ induces a functor $f_{*}:{\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{B}\to{\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{C}$. Specifically, given a $B$ -comodule $M$ with structure map $\delta:M\to M\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B$, the $C$ -comodule $f_{*}M$ has the same underlying $\mathbf{k}$ -vector space as $M$ and has structure map $(\mathrm{id}_{M}\otimes f)\circ\delta:M\to M\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}C$.
card.label: Example 2.5

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
